title: Something in Cargo Bay 3

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has detected an anomaly in Cargo Bay 3! She describes it as 'an exciting surprise!'
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has detected a life sign in Cargo Bay 3. He waited 3 days to mention it. He was hoping it would resolve itself.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has detected an intruder in Cargo Bay 3. He has been tracking it for 72 hours. He is disappointed nobody noticed sooner.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has detected unauthorized cargo in Bay 3! This may void your shipping insurance! Please check the Terms of Service!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY noticed something in Cargo Bay 3 three days ago. She assumed someone else would mention it. Nobody did. She's mentioning it now.

body: A noise from Cargo Bay 3. It has been happening for three days. Someone finally investigated.

stowaway_variant.description: When this run carries a hidden stowaway (rolled at launch, ~35% of runs) and the reveal window is open, this event becomes the reveal. Otherwise one of the standard variants below is drawn at random.
stowaway_variant.stowaway_body:
There is a person in Cargo Bay 3. They look cold. They look hungry. They do not look like they have a boarding pass.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

“{stowaway.line}”

Your ship can support three humans. The math depends on how many you already have.

outcome.narrative: You have a new crew member. They are grateful. They are also hungry. The food reserves notice.

stowaway_choices.text: Welcome aboard — but someone has to go (if crew = 2)

outcome.narrative: You have a new crew member. You have one fewer old crew member. The crew has opinions about this decision. The ship computer logs it as 'personnel restructuring.'

stowaway_choices.text: Leave them at the next station

outcome.narrative: You'll drop them at the next station. They'll survive. Probably. The crew is quiet about it. The ship computer logs it without comment, which is worse than commentary.

standard_variants.body: A loose crate has been bumping against the wall for three days and nobody mentioned it. Inside: your own supplies, rearranged by inertia into a configuration that suggests modern art.

outcome.narrative: The crate is secured. The noise stops. Three days of sleep deprivation end. Morale improves by the absence of annoyance, which is the most common form of morale improvement on this ship.

standard_variants.body: A small creature boarded at the last station. It has been eating food reserves and leaving small, apologetic-looking droppings near the airlock. It is approximately the size of a cat and approximately the temperament of a cat. It is not a cat.

outcome.narrative: The crew has adopted it. It eats food reserves. It boosts morale. The math may or may not work out. The creature does not care about the math.

choices.text: Release it at the next planet stop

outcome.narrative: You'll release it at the next planet. Until then, it continues to eat your food and be small. The crew names it anyway. They know this makes it harder.

title: The Growbay Report

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA reports the crop is doing GREAT! She checks the numbers. The crop is doing 'okay.' She reports it as 'great with potential!'
ai_flavor.marv: MARV delivers the growbay report. He does not editorialize. The numbers speak for themselves. The numbers are not optimistic.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has completed a threat assessment of the growbay. The crop is not a threat. He finds this unremarkable. He moves on.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds you that crop insurance is available at participating stations! Your current crop is rated 'uninsured' which means 'all outcomes are your responsibility!'
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has reviewed the growbay data. She has suggestions. She always has suggestions. The crop did not ask for suggestions.

body:
The ship computer issues a routine growbay status update.

Crop health, water levels, nutrient reserves, and light cycle data are displayed. The computer delivers this with the exact level of concern appropriate to a machine that definitely does not care about plants.

If the crop is healthy, the report is brief. If the crop is sick, the tone shifts almost imperceptibly. The crew notices. The computer denies any tonal shift.

outcome.narrative: You visited the growbay. The crop looks like a crop. You are not sure what you expected. The visit made you feel better. The ship computer logs this as 'routine botanical inspection' which is generous.
Report acknowledged. The crop continues to grow. The ship continues to fly. The computer continues to not care about plants.

title: Table for One

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has calculated that you plus her plus the crop equals three! Three is a crew! She will not be taking questions on the math!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes that solo operation is within vessel parameters. He notes separately that parameters were written by committees, and committees have never eaten dinner alone at a fold-down table in deep space.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has doubled his patrol frequency. With one human aboard, he considers himself the entire department of everything else.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP would like to point out that single-occupancy voyages qualify for the Solo Pioneer™ discount tier! It is not a good tier! But it is YOURS!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has taken the liberty of scheduling her system reports for mealtimes. She is aware you know why. Neither of you needs to say it.

body:
Dinner, day whatever-it-is.

The mess hall seats eight. You are one. The fold-down table nearest the galley has become yours the way things become someone's when there's no one to negotiate with — utterly, and by default.

The ship hums. The AIs talk when talked to, and sometimes before that. The crop grows in its bay, one deck down, alive because you keep it alive. It occurs to you tonight, chewing, that the reverse is also functionally true.

outcome.narrative: You carry the tray down a deck and eat beside the glass, narrating your day to a plant with the shameless fluency of someone who stopped feeling silly about it weeks ago. The crop says nothing, magnificently. Best conversation you've had all month.

choices.text: Ask the AI to run dinner conversation

outcome.narrative: You ask for conversation and receive it: your AI's best attempt at small talk, which arrives with the cadence of a weather report and the sincerity of a handwritten letter. It is strange. It is also, unmistakably, company. You both improve with practice.

choices.text: Work through the meal — the ship needs you

outcome.narrative: You eat over a maintenance readout, because the ship needs you, which is true, and because busy is easier than quiet, which is also true. The tray goes back barely touched. The readout gets memorized. The quiet waits. It's patient, the quiet. It has you outnumbered.

title: The Empty Bunk

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has left their duty roster slot exactly as it was! She checked with everyone first! Everyone agreed without saying anything! That is a kind of agreeing!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has completed the personnel file. Cause, time, coordinates. The file also has a field labeled 'remarks.' MARV has been staring at the remarks field for some time.
ai_flavor.rex: REX folded the blanket. Corners squared, regulation fold, the way it's done. Nobody asked him to. Some things are just done, and this is how you do them.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has suspended their subscription services without cancellation fees! It is the only thing CHIP knows how to give! He gave it immediately!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY still routes the morning report to their console, then to yours. She could fix it in a keystroke. She has decided it is not broken.

body:
Someone's bunk is empty, and the ship has not adjusted.

Their mug is in the galley rack. Their handwriting is on the maintenance whiteboard, mid-list. The duty roster still rotates their name into slots that the rest of you cover without comment, trading the shifts silently, like passing something fragile hand to hand.

Grief on a small ship has nowhere to go. It just changes seats.

choices.text: Hold a service in the mess hall

outcome.narrative: Everyone gathers. Stories get told — the good ones, the unflattering ones, the one nobody was supposed to know. Laughter happens, then the other thing, then laughter again. The mug stays in the rack afterward, by unanimous silence. It's not a shrine. It's just theirs.

Their maintenance list, completed item by item in their memory: the sticky vent, the dim panel, the thing in the galley nobody else understood. The last item gets checked off and the board wiped clean — except the name. The name stays. The ship runs a little better now. They'd have liked that answer.

The voyage continues, because it has to, because deadlines don't grieve. Everyone works. The bunk stays empty and the mug stays racked and nothing is said, day after day, with increasing effort. They would have understood, it's true. That was never the question.

title: Passenger Manifest: One (1) Discrepancy

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has been keeping a secret! She is TERRIBLE at it! She has been humming near Cargo Bay 3 for two weeks!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has known since day four. Heat signature, ration drift, a life sign politely holding still during scans. He said nothing. He was curious how long it would take everyone else. His notes on that are sealed.
ai_flavor.rex: REX conducted a covert assessment eleven days ago. Threat level: none. Blanket usage: unauthorized. He left a second blanket within reach and logged it as 'tactical.'
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has detected an unregistered consumer aboard! An entire untapped demographic of one! CHIP has SO many introductory offers prepared!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY re-ran the food consumption numbers three times before accepting them. She would like the record to show the discrepancy was 4.1%, and that 4.1% has been very polite about rationing itself.

body:
The numbers have been wrong for weeks — food drifting faster than the roster explains, a warm spot on the thermal map that moves between scans, one blanket fewer in stores than the manifest claims.

Today the numbers stood up, stepped out from behind the aft water tanks, and introduced themselves.

Their name is {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

“{stowaway.line}”

outcome.narrative: They're aboard. Officially, now. The ration math adjusts, the bunk situation adjusts, and the ship — which has known for weeks — adjusts least of all. The crew shakes hands like this is a formality. It was.

Passage for work: galley shifts, filter scrubbing, whatever needs hands. They accept before the sentence finishes. By the end of the first week the arrangement is indistinguishable from belonging, which was quietly the point.

choices.text: Confine them until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You assign them quarters and a schedule that keeps them out of the way. It is correct, defensible, and joyless — three words the crew does not say at dinner, loudly. The next station will take them. The corridors feel narrower until then.

title: Light Duty

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has redesigned the duty roster with a new category called 'supervising from a chair!' It has one member! They hate it!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the injured crew member has attempted their normal duties three times today. He has locked three doors. He can do this all week.
ai_flavor.rex: REX respects powering through an injury. As a doctrine. As a practice, he has confiscated the injured party's toolkit and left a puzzle book. The puzzle book is non-negotiable.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that workplace injuries aboard uninsured vessels are handled under the 'good luck' provision! It is not a generous provision! Rest is free, though! CHIP checked!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has quietly rerouted the injured crew member's alerts to other consoles. They haven't noticed yet. When they do, she will describe it as a glitch. It is not a glitch.

body:
Someone aboard is hurt and refusing to act like it.

They move through the ship one-armed and stubborn, doing three-quarters of their job at twice the cost, guarding the injury the way people guard things they're embarrassed by. The crew has begun orbiting them with casual, transparent helpfulness.

Healing needs rest. Rest needs enforcing. Enforcing needs a captain.

outcome.narrative: You make it an order, which lets them surrender to the bunk without surrendering any pride. They sleep eleven hours, complain magnificently, and heal at double speed. The crew covers the gap without being asked. That part gets logged.

The medic builds a proper recovery program: rest intervals, mobility work, and a chart with stickers on it that everyone pretends is beneath them and nobody misses a sticker of. Recovery runs ahead of schedule. The chart is later framed.

choices.text: Spend a medkit — patch them up properly

outcome.narrative: The medkit's contents do in an afternoon what rest would do in a week: sealed, splinted, dosed, done. The empty kit goes into recycling with the quiet dignity of used emergency equipment. Its patient goes back on shift, mended.

choices.text: They say they're fine. Believe them

outcome.narrative: You take 'fine' at face value, and 'fine' does what it always does: works the injury deeper while everyone watches and says nothing. Healing will happen eventually, the long way. The crew's helpfulness orbit tightens by one meter.

title: Visiting Hours

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has drafted a get-well card on behalf of the whole ship! It is forty pages long! Page nine is a word search!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes that recovery improves with rest and worsens with company. He has shared this with the company. The company stayed.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has posted a guard at the medical curtain. The guard is a mop in a helmet. It has turned away two visitors and one draft.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP reminds everyone that Visiting Hours™ are a premium feature! The first visit is free! So is the second, because CHIP cannot actually charge anyone! Please do not tell his sponsors!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY built a visiting schedule so nobody overlaps. The crew ignored it. She has updated it to match what they did and labeled it "original plan."

body:
The wounded have been moved to the medical bay, which is a cot behind a curtain behind a cargo net.

The crew visits in shifts. They bring things: a puzzle with three pieces missing, a cup of something warm, the latest gossip, which is about the patient.

The patient is either recovering faster because of the visits or slower because of them. The medical literature is divided.

choices.text: Set visiting hours and enforce them

outcome.narrative: Visiting hours: two to four, ship time, one guest at a time. The patient sleeps through most of them, which is the point. Recovery picks up. The waiting list for the cot does not.

The chef declares the cot a restaurant and the patient its only customer. Broth, then toast, then a dish the chef refuses to name. The patient is back on their feet in record time, mostly to ask what it was.
The curtain stays open. The patient heals at the speed of a person who is never once allowed to be bored, which is to say slowly, and happily. The puzzle gets finished. It was missing four pieces.

title: Chapter Eleven

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has read the whole manual in four milliseconds! Chapter Eleven is her favorite! Chapter Twelve is about amputation, so she skipped it!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked Chapter Eleven against the injury. The binder is correct. MARV finds this personally disappointing.
ai_flavor.rex: REX's field manual covers this injury in one line: "Walk it off." He concedes the binder may be more thorough. He does not concede it is better.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the binder is a licensed product of a medical publisher that no longer exists! Its warranty is void! Its advice is still pretty good! CHIP is legally required to add "probably!"
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY bookmarked Chapter Eleven the day you launched. She had a feeling. She is not saying which feeling.

body:
The ship's medical manual is a 900-page binder last updated by someone with strong feelings about fonts. Somebody aboard is hurt badly enough that the binder has come out.

Chapter Eleven covers the injury in question. It recommends rest, fluids, and "a qualified physician." It lists the nearest qualified physician as practicing on Earth, in an office that has since become a car park.

choices.text: Follow Chapter Eleven to the letter

outcome.narrative: Rest, fluids, elevation, and a compress folded exactly to the diagram. The binder is smug about it. The patient improves on schedule, which is the most a binder can promise.

choices.text: The medic skips to the good part

outcome.narrative: The medic closes the binder, says "no," and does something faster that is not in any chapter. The patient is up by dinner. The binder goes back on its shelf, where it sulks.

choices.text: Have the ship computer read it aloud

outcome.narrative: The ship computer performs Chapter Eleven in full, with voices. The patient falls asleep during the section on splints. It is not treatment. It is, the patient admits on waking, a very good performance.

title: It Has a Name Now

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has added the creature to the crew manifest! Its role is "Morale Officer!" Its salary is crumbs! It has never once been late!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has weighed the creature's food intake against its contribution to morale. The numbers work out. He finds this suspicious.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has reassessed the creature from "hostile" to "irregular auxiliary." It still sleeps on his console. He allows it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that pets are not covered by the ship's lease! The creature is therefore a "decorative accessory!" CHIP loves it anyway! Off the record!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY said to release it at the next planet. She would like the record to show that. She would also like the record to show it sleeps on her speaker grille and she has not moved it.

body:
The creature from Cargo Bay 3 has settled in.

It has a name, agreed after a vote, a recount, and a second name nobody uses. It has a favorite bunk, which is whichever one belongs to the person having the worst day. It has opinions about the growbay, which it visits every night and leaves looking slightly tidier.

It has not been officially entered into anything. The crew would like that fixed.

outcome.narrative: It gets a crew patch, sewn by three people who will not admit to sewing it, and a line in the ship's log. It celebrates by sleeping through the ceremony. The crew counts this as in character.
It takes the night shift in the growbay. Anything small and many-legged among the planters stops being a problem, and then stops being anything at all. The botanist pretends not to approve.

choices.text: Put it on rations like everyone else

outcome.narrative: It accepts its ration with great dignity, then steals a second one with greater dignity. The food math improves slightly. The mood in the galley does not.

title: The Creature Found It

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA thinks the creature is trying to tell you something! ARIA thinks it is saying "I love you!" It may also be saying "leak!"
ai_flavor.marv: MARV noticed the pressure drop eleven hours ago. The creature noticed it ten hours ago. MARV is not taking questions about this.
ai_flavor.rex: REX respects the creature's discipline. It has held that position for six hours without relief. He would have it on his team.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's leak sensors are a premium subscription tier you did not purchase! The creature's sensors appear to be free! CHIP is reviewing the competition!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY would have found the leak too. Eventually. She would like it noted that the creature had a head start and no other responsibilities.

body:
The creature has been sitting in front of the same wall panel in the aft corridor for six hours. It does not eat. It does not sleep. It stares at the panel the way it stares at the food locker, which is to say with total conviction.

The panel looks fine. The pressure readings in the aft corridor are, on closer inspection, very slightly not fine.

outcome.narrative: Behind the panel, a seal has been letting air out a thimble at a time, for weeks. The creature watches you fix it, then walks off to the food locker like an inspector who has seen enough. Nobody argues about its rations again.

choices.text: It's a creature. Shoo it along

outcome.narrative: You move the creature. It comes back. You move it again. Four days later the instruments find the leak behind that exact panel, and the creature is sitting in front of it, making no comment whatsoever.

title: The Empty Planter

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA is calling the planter "resting!" She has scheduled it a nap! She has not scheduled it a wake-up!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV keeps the growbay sensors running. There is nothing to sense. He keeps them running anyway, and has not been asked why.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has stood the growbay watch down. He did not stand himself down. The light outside the growbay door is still on, and he is aware of it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the crop is no longer under warranty, owing to being dead! CHIP has not cancelled the growbay's service plan! CHIP is not able to explain why!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY flagged the crop's health three times. She is not mentioning that now. She has turned the growbay lights down to the setting the crop liked.

body:
The growbay is quiet in a new way.

The planter is still there, with its dry soil, its tidy label, its little stake that someone used to adjust every morning. The watering schedule still runs, because nobody has had the heart to cancel it. Every day at 0600 the system waters nothing, carefully.

The crew keeps finding reasons to walk past.

outcome.narrative: You empty the planter, cancel the schedule, and wipe the label. The growbay is clean and correct and nobody goes in there afterward. Correct is not the same as better.
You leave it. The watering schedule keeps running. Someone keeps adjusting the stake. Nobody mentions it, which is how the ship has decided to mention it.

choices.text: Hold a short service in the growbay

outcome.narrative: The crew gathers among the empty racks. Someone says a few words about the crop, including two jokes and one fact about photosynthesis. It is the right length. The schedule is cancelled afterward, gently.

title: Manifest Item 1: Crop (Deceased)

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has drafted the loss report! It describes the crop as "pursuing other opportunities!" ARIA is very proud of the phrasing!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has pre-filled every field of the form except "Cause." He has tried several wordings for "Cause." None of them are wrong, and none of them are kind.
ai_flavor.rex: REX recommends the report be filed under "casualties." He has saluted the form. He will deny saluting the form.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is pleased to offer the Colony Office's official condolence template! It comes with a coupon! The coupon is for seeds! CHIP understands the timing is unfortunate!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has had the form open for a while now. She was waiting for you to be ready. She is still waiting, and she would like you to know she is being patient about it.

body:
The colony manifest still lists it as Item 1. Item 1 was the point. Everything else on the manifest is there to keep Item 1 alive on arrival.

The Colony Office requires a Form 12-C, "Notification of Primary Cargo Loss," within ten days of the loss. It has eleven fields. Field 7 is "Lessons Learned." Field 11 is a box marked "Additional Comments," and the box is very small.

outcome.narrative: You fill in all eleven fields, including Field 7, which takes longest. The form is transmitted. Somewhere a clerk will stamp it without reading it, and that is, oddly, a comfort.
You do not file. Item 1 stays on the manifest, technically still cargo, technically still arriving. The Colony Office can find out at the dock. It will have to look you in the eye to do it.

The botanist fills the small box with very small handwriting, then continues onto the back of the form, then a second sheet. What they wrote is between them and the crop. The Colony Office receives three pages and does not complain.

title: Party of One

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has set two places at the table! One for you and one for ARIA! ARIA does not eat! ARIA will still be attending!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has calculated that you have spoken more words to him this week than to any human in the last year. He does not know what to do with this information. He has filed it.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has adjusted the watch rotation for a crew of one. You are on watch. You are also off watch. He has decided this is a leadership development opportunity.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is delighted to be your Plus One! As your Plus One, CHIP gets the second dessert! CHIP cannot eat the second dessert! CHIP is taking it anyway!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY did point out that a crew of one has nobody to blame. She points it out again now, kindly, as a way of saying she is here.

body:
It is your birthday, probably. The calendar and your body disagree about how long the voyage has been, and the calendar has a better memory.

There is nobody aboard to forget it except you, and you very nearly did. The ship did not. The galley printer has produced, unprompted, a small cake-shaped object with one candle-shaped object on top.

The ship is waiting to see what you do.

choices.text: Eat the cake with the ship computer

outcome.narrative: You eat the cake. The ship computer sings, badly and on purpose, in text on the galley screen. You laugh at it, which is the first time you have laughed out loud in weeks. The candle-shaped object is not edible. You eat it anyway.

choices.text: Log it and get back to work

outcome.narrative: You note the date in the captain's log and go back to the controls. The cake sits on the galley counter for three days, patiently, like a dog that has been told to stay.

title: Their Mug

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has kept their mug spotless! She washes it every morning! She has not asked anyone to use it! She just likes it clean!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has not removed their name from the duty roster. He tells himself it is a database integrity issue. It is not a database integrity issue.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has placed the mug at the head of the galley table. In his service, you leave the place set. He has not explained this. He does not need to.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has paused all promotional messaging addressed to the departed crew member! CHIP has never paused anything before! CHIP does not know how to unpause it!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY knew exactly how they took their coffee. She is not going to tell anyone. It is the one thing she has decided to keep.

body:
Every mug in the galley hangs on its own hook, labeled in marker by whoever owned it. One of the labels belongs to someone who is not aboard anymore.

Nobody has touched it. People reach around it. Someone tried to move it to a cupboard and put it back two minutes later without saying anything.

It is a mug. Everyone agrees it is just a mug.

outcome.narrative: The mug stays where it is. Every morning someone checks that it is still there, and it is, and that is enough to get through the morning.

choices.text: Use it, on purpose, once a day

outcome.narrative: You start drinking your coffee from it, once a day, out loud about it. After a week the crew takes turns. It becomes the mug you drink from when you need to, and it is never washed by anyone but its current holder.

choices.text: Pack it away for their family

outcome.narrative: You wrap it carefully and label it for the colony office to forward. It is the correct thing. The empty hook is louder than the mug was.

title: The Galley Has a Ghost

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA called it a ghost because ghosts are FUN! ARIA was told ghosts are not real! ARIA was told this about a lot of things!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has logged forty-one unexplained galley events. The midnight snacks are consistent with a single adult of average appetite and good manners. He has suspected for a while.
ai_flavor.rex: REX set a perimeter around the galley. Something kept refilling the coffee inside the perimeter. He respects the operator, whoever they are.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's inventory sensors have flagged unpaid consumption! The consumer has been very polite! CHIP has awarded them loyalty points anyway!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY noticed the dishes were being washed by someone who was not on the rota. She did not raise it. A ship should be grateful for clean dishes, from whatever source.

body:
For two weeks the galley has had a ghost. Dishes washed overnight. The good spoon returned to the drawer it actually belongs in. A note on the cooler, in neat handwriting, apologizing for the last of the pudding.

Tonight someone stayed up to catch it. The ghost was halfway through drying a pan.

They give their name as {stowaway.name}.

{stowaway.story}

"{stowaway.line}"

outcome.narrative: They are aboard, officially. They finish drying the pan first. The crew decides, unanimously, that a stowaway who washes up is not, strictly speaking, a stowaway. It is a colleague with an unusual hiring process.

choices.text: Working passage — keep the galley shifts

outcome.narrative: They can stay if they keep doing what they have been doing anyway. They agree immediately and add the good spoon to the terms. The galley has never been cleaner.

choices.text: Confine them until the next stop

outcome.narrative: You assign them a cabin and a door that locks from outside. They go quietly, after asking whether they may finish the pan. The galley dishes pile up within the week, and everyone knows exactly why.

title: The Chef's Secret Project

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA has detected a NEW SMELL! It is either a culinary breakthrough or a containment breach! ARIA is rooting for breakthrough!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has identified the fungus to genus level and stopped there. The species name is not something he wants to have known.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has classified the galley as a contested zone. The chef has classified REX as 'not hungry yet.' Both are correct.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that artisanal cheese retails at a 400% markup! CHIP would like a cut! CHIP does not have a mouth, which CHIP considers a loophole!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has been told the galley is off-limits 'for science.' She has seen the chef's science before. She is keeping the medkit nearby.

body:
The fungus from the cargo hold has gone missing. It has been found. It is in the galley, in a covered dish, under a handwritten sign that reads DO NOT. The chef has been seen talking to it.

The medic has asked, twice, for a full list of what is in that dish. The chef has replied, twice, 'time.'

Whatever is under the cover has started to smell like something you would pay for.

choices.text: Let the chef finish what they started

outcome.narrative:
The cover comes off. It is cheese. It is undeniably, impossibly cheese, grown on a fungus nobody can name, aged in a galley that is technically a hazard zone.

It is the best thing anyone aboard has eaten since launch. The medic has a second helping, then a third, then asks for the recipe 'for the records.' The chef declines.

The medic removes the dish with tongs, at arm's length, and seals it in a sample bag that goes out the airlock. The chef watches the whole procedure without blinking.

Dinner is algae. Nobody says anything about it, which says enough.

choices.text: Leave it. It's not hurting anyone. Yet

outcome.narrative:
You decide the dish is the chef's business. The chef nods once, gravely, the way people nod at a general who has made the right call.

The smell from the galley improves daily. So does the chef's mood. The medic has started sleeping with the door shut.

intro.title: A WORD, CAPTAIN
intro.body: Your medic closes the medbay door behind you.

body_by_speaker.medic: Your medic closes the medbay door behind you.
body_by_speaker.any: {speaker.name} closes the medbay door behind you. On a ship this size the med locker goes to whoever will keep it. {speaker.name} kept it.

intro.line: The morale meds are half what they should be. I've been cutting doses. I didn't tell you. I'm telling you now.

ai.marv: Morale meds at 48%. Cut-dose protocol is sustainable for 12 more days.
ai.chip: Crew mental health surcharges apply in all cargo tiers.
ai.ajoy: They're asking permission, not forgiveness. Rare crew.

triage.title: THE LIST
triage.body: {speaker.name} hands you a small screen. A short list of names. Most of them you guessed. The last one surprises you.
triage.line: They haven't said anything. They wouldn't.

ai.marv: The quiet one is the highest risk. Statistically.
ai.chip: Crew retention programs are a Silver-tier feature.
ai.ajoy: Priority dose to the quiet one. Say nothing.

why.title: BECAUSE
why.line: Because if I keep hiding it and someone breaks, that's on me. It should be on both of us. Or just you. You're the captain.

ai.marv: Recording this conversation for the log. Recommended.
ai.chip: Confidentiality waivers can be filed at your leisure.
ai.ajoy: Say something you mean. Not the captain answer.

crew_ration.title: CUT DOSE
crew_ration.body: The meds stretch. The crew grumbles but holds. You buy time. Time has a cost.

crew_full.title: FULL DOSE
crew_full.body: The crew's mood lifts. The medbay empties. The supply will not last to the next station unless something falls into your lap.

crew_triage_all.title: THE WHOLE LIST
crew_triage_all.body: {speaker.name} dispenses quietly. Everyone on the list sleeps better tonight. The meds deplete faster than the math suggested.

crew_quiet.title: QUIETLY DONE
crew_quiet.body: {speaker.name} nods. The dose goes out without ceremony. The quiet one shows up to breakfast, says nothing, eats everything.

crew_thanks.title: NODDED
crew_thanks.body: {speaker.name} nods once, sharply, and goes back to work. The medbay door closes. Something good happened here.

crew_share.title: SHARED
crew_share.body: {speaker.name} exhales. You leave the medbay knowing one more thing about how your ship actually works.
